Median not separately visible in 11 of 30 boxes: a1 RiskAgent-8B (Q1 edge, 73.25; box 73.25-76.06); a1 GPT-4o (Q3 edge, 59.13; box 57.74-59.13); a1 o3-mini (Q3 edge, 57.72; box 57.04-57.72); a2 GPT-4o (Q1 edge, 51.57; box 51.57-53.16); a2 o3-mini (Q1 edge, 53.18; box 53.18-53.79); a3 GPT-4o (Q3 edge, 50.18; box 50.08-50.18); a4 RiskAgent-8B (Q3 edge, 71.79; box 70.66-71.79); a5 GPT-4o (Q3 edge, 50.62; box 50.55-50.62); b1 RiskAgent-8B (Q1 edge, 77.46; box 77.46-78.15); b2 o3-mini (Q1 edge, 58.54; box 58.54-60.10); b5 GPT-4o (Q3 edge, 38.35; box 38.12-38.35). In these the median line coincides with the Q1 or Q3 edge (five runs, quartiles = 2nd and 4th value, ties are common because accuracies are k/N). Which edge was decided with the paper's Table 1 (mean over the same five runs), not from the pixels; these rows carry confidence 0.75. A model that reads only the figure cannot know the edge. Where the box is tall the table decides clearly: a1 RiskAgent-8B (73.25, the other edge is 76.06); a1 GPT-4o (59.13, the other edge is 57.74); a1 o3-mini (57.72, the other edge is 57.04); a2 GPT-4o (51.57, the other edge is 53.16); a2 o3-mini (53.18, the other edge is 53.79); a4 RiskAgent-8B (71.79, the other edge is 70.66); b1 RiskAgent-8B (77.46, the other edge is 78.15); b2 o3-mini (58.54, the other edge is 60.10). There a prediction of the box centre or of the other edge is off by up to 10% of the axis range (a1 RiskAgent-8B: 2.8 of 27.5 units) and should not be read as a misreading; set these values to null if only pixel-readable medians are to be scored. Where the box is thin (a3 GPT-4o (50.08-50.18); a5 GPT-4o (50.55-50.62); b5 GPT-4o (38.12-38.35)) the table cannot separate the edges, but either edge is within 0.25 units (under 0.5% of the axis range) of the recorded value.

Cross-check with Table 1 (page 5; mean and SD over five runs): taking (lower whisker end or lower outlier, Q1, median, Q3, upper whisker end or upper outlier) as the five runs, the mean of every one of the 30 boxes reproduces the table to within 0.04 (average gap 0.013) and the population SD to within 0.02. For the Stroke/TIA panels the measured lines also sit on multiples of 1/142 (e.g. 71.12, 73.25, 76.06, 76.77 = 101, 104, 108, 109 of 142) to within 0.04.

Thin boxes (a3 GPT-4o, a5 GPT-4o, b2 RiskAgent-8B, b3 GPT-4o, b5 GPT-4o) are 0-0.35 units tall; their lines merge into one black band and were separated by the stroke width (0.42 pt). The quartiles there are good to about +/- 0.05, which is far inside the scorer's tolerance.

Tick labels and model names are text objects without a usable Unicode map (the text layer returns blanks), so the y tick values were read from a 12x render and matched one-to-one to the vector major ticks; the y titles are printed vertically in blue. No unit is printed on the axes (the paper reports accuracy in %).

Series: no legend; one series per panel named after the y-axis title (the scorer ignores series names when both sides have one series). Category = the model name under each box. Panel titles combine the row heading and the y-axis title; neither is printed as a per-panel title.

Panel ids a1-a5, b1-b5 (row letter + column); bbox_px covers each panel's axes, tick labels and y title, not the row headings 'a. MedRisk-Qualitative' / 'b. MedRisk-Quantitative'. figure.bbox is copied verbatim from the picture's prov in document.json (l, t, r, b with coord_origin BOTTOMLEFT, as in the existing truth files); bbox_px is in pixels of the bundle crop.
